attacksRun.evidence: The gating test, and I ran it against live harness bytes rather than against my own v1 text. SF1 demanded each of the three classes carry at least one named initial state DRAWN FROM G16 v2's exactByteIntent, with the NOT-AUTHORED markers attached to those named states rather than to the class name. v2 carries 12 states: change-impact-matrix 5, forced-mutations 5, aggregate-release 2 — every class covered, every stateNamed distinct. Each was traced to the live exactByteIntent of its own class and 12/12 are present there verbatim: 'add/delete/rename/byte-change units' supplies the four change-set units; 'An unrelated change does not force every language closure to build' supplies the fifth; 'omitted dependency, omitted owner, missing component declaration, owner outside the comparison-basis universe, and incomplete or invalid universe construction' supplies all five mutation kinds; 'a component-new/core-unchanged selection and a core-new/component-unchanged selection' supplies both release selections. Every record now carries stateNamed plus a source field citing the originating exactByteIntent, and fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED hangs off that named state. The v1 shape was four fields (id, memberVerbatim, fixtureBytes, assertsNamedNotAuthored); v2 carries eight. SF1 is landed, and landed with precisely the material SF1 identified as available.

attacksRun.attack: the platform axis is listed as all four D-002 platforms without the live manifest-scope rider (my own attack)
attacksRun.evidence: The sharpest residual attack. Live change-impact exactByteIntent scopes cells to 'that identity's manifest-declared D-002 platforms' and adds 'platform scope follows the component manifest'; the four change-impact states each carry a flat platforms list of all four D-002 values with no manifest rider reproduced. I decline to charge it: the four values ARE enumerated verbatim in the live intent, so the axis is drawn not invented; the artifact names no component identity at all, so there is no manifest to follow yet and nothing is resolved against one; and it nowhere asserts that every component declares all four. The governing rider and passProperty live in G16 v2 and the named catalog, both pinned here at verified digests. Recorded so a later fixture-authoring cycle carries the manifest-scope rider forward rather than reading the flat list as a requirement.

attacksRun.attack: per-state field shape is inconsistent across the three classes (my own attack)
attacksRun.evidence: languageRole and platforms appear on the change-impact states, languageRole alone on the unrelated-change state, and neither on the forced-mutations or aggregate-release states. I checked whether this is sloppiness and it is not: it tracks the live source. change-impact's exactByteIntent is the only one carrying a language-role and platform axis; the unrelated-change sentence is about language closures and not per-platform cells; and neither forced-mutations nor aggregate-release names a platform or language axis in its live intent. The heterogeneity is evidence the states were drawn rather than templated. Observation, not a finding.
